Thanks Ben — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Residency: ACME prefers customer data (request payloads and logs) to remain in the US only. We may request EU residency for some European merchant accounts later, but initial deployment should be US.
2) Retention: We need to confirm retention windows for request/response logs and any debug logs. Is there a configurable retention policy per account?
3) Logging controls: We need to know what logs Redwood maintains by default (request bodies, model prompts, generated outputs, system logs) and what can be disabled or masked. Does Redwood support automatic PII redaction in logs or a way to exclude sensitive fields?
4) Roles: Please confirm that ACME is the controller and Redwood is the processor for hosted API usage, and how subprocessors are handled (pre-notify + objection window?).
5) Breach notice: Our legal prefers 48 hours for initial notice of confirmed breaches impacting ACME data. Is that feasible?

Tom may push back on certain language, so I copied him. We'll send a redline after your replies. If you can get answers by tomorrow end of day, that would help procurement timelines.

—Alice Turner

Hi all — thanks for the details, Ben and Alice. Below are concise answers we can include in a follow-up note / FAQ. Marissa — I included a couple of legal notes below; happy to adapt language for a redline.

1) Data residency: 
- Redwood supports single-region tenancy. We can provision ACME to keep customer payloads and logs in us-east-1 only. For future EU accounts we can provision separate tenancy in eu-west-1.

2) Retention & configurable policy: 
- Per-account retention is configurable via the Console or API. Default retention for request/response logs is 90 days. We can shorten this to 30 days or set custom retention for enterprise accounts via policy (will reflect in the DPA/SLA).

3) Logging controls & PII handling: 
- By default Redwood captures minimal request metadata and full request/response payloads for debugging and quality monitoring. Customers may enable "redaction" at ingest to mask fields (JSON key patterns) and can disable storing request bodies — in that mode we only retain non-identifying telemetry.
- We also offer a managed PII redaction add-on that applies regex and field-based rules pre-storage. Details are in the security whitepaper (attached link).

4) Roles (controller/processor): 
- For hosted API usage: ACME is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor. This is consistent with our DPA. We process data per ACME's documented instructions and do not use customer payloads to train models unless explicitly opted-in in writing.

5) Subprocessors: 
- Redwood maintains a subprocessors list in our transparency portal. We provide 30 days advance notice for adding new subprocessors that will process customer data; customers have a right to object within that window for lawful reasons. Critical cloud infra providers are listed and covered.

6) Breach notice timing: 
- Redwood's standard commitment is to provide initial notice of confirmed incidents affecting customer data within 72 hours. We understand ACME's preference for 48 hours; operationally, 48 hours is challenging for initial confirmed notices for large-scale incidents because of investigation time, but we can commit to prioritized response and aim to provide an initial engagement update within 48 hours with a confirmed incident report within 72 hours. We are open to discussing a contractual 48-hour SLA for certain incident classes under an enterprise addendum (subject to insurance/response commitments).

Attachments and links: Redwood_DPA_clean.pdf (attached), Redwood_DPA_redline_ACME.docx (we can produce a starter redline if you provide target clauses), security_whitepaper.pdf, and a DocuSign link if you'd like an execution-ready copy.

- Marissa/Legal: if ACME provides a redline, we'll produce a Redwood response within 2 business days.

If helpful, I'm available for a 30-minute technical/legal sync tomorrow morning.
